heading_path: Short Title
own_text: This Act may be cited as the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act .

heading_path: Interpretation
Interpretation
own_text: The definitions in this subsection apply in this Act. Board means the Immigration and Refugee Board, which consists of the Refugee Protection Division, Refugee Appeal Division, Immigration Division and Immigration Appeal Division. ( Commission ) Convention Against Torture means the Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment, signed at New York on December 10, 1984. Article 1 of the Convention Against Torture is set out in the schedule. ( Convention contre la torture ) designated foreign national has the meaning assigned by subsection 20.1(2). ( étranger désigné ) foreign national means a person who is not a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident, and includes a stateless person. ( étranger ) permanent resident means a person who has acquired permanent resident status and has not subsequently lost that status under section 46. ( résident permanent ) prescribed means prescribed by regulation. ( Version anglaise seulement ) Refugee Convention means the United Nations Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, signed at Geneva on July 28, 1951, and the Protocol to that Convention, signed at New York on January 31, 1967. Sections E and F of Article 1 of the Refugee Convention are set out in the schedule. ( Convention sur les réfugiés )

heading_path: Interpretation
own_text: Unless otherwise indicated, references in this Act to “this Act” include regulations made under it and instructions given under subsection 14.1(1).

heading_path: Objectives and Application
Objectives and Application
own_text: The objectives of this Act with respect to immigration are

label: (a)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to permit Canada to pursue the maximum social, cultural and economic benefits of immigration;

label: (b)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to enrich and strengthen the social and cultural fabric of Canadian society, while respecting the federal, bilingual and multicultural character of Canada;

label: (b.1)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to support and assist the development of minority official languages communities in Canada;

label: (c)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to support the development of a strong and prosperous Canadian economy, in which the benefits of immigration are shared across all regions of Canada;

label: (d)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to see that families are reunited in Canada;

label: (e)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to promote the successful integration of permanent residents into Canada, while recognizing that integration involves mutual obligations for new immigrants and Canadian society;

label: (f)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to support, by means of consistent standards and prompt processing, the attainment of immigration goals established by the Government of Canada in consultation with the provinces;

label: (f.1)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to maintain, through the establishment of fair and efficient procedures, the integrity of the Canadian immigration system;

label: (g)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to facilitate the entry of visitors, students and temporary workers for purposes such as trade, commerce, tourism, international understanding and cultural, educational and scientific activities;

label: (h)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to protect public health and safety and to maintain the security of Canadian society;

label: (i)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to promote international justice and security by fostering respect for human rights and by denying access to Canadian territory to persons who are criminals or security risks; and

label: (j)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to work in cooperation with the provinces to secure better recognition of the foreign credentials of permanent residents and their more rapid integration into society.

heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: The objectives of this Act with respect to refugees are

label: (a)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to recognize that the refugee program is in the first instance about saving lives and offering protection to the displaced and persecuted;

label: (b)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to fulfil Canada’s international legal obligations with respect to refugees and affirm Canada’s commitment to international efforts to provide assistance to those in need of resettlement;

label: (c)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to grant, as a fundamental expression of Canada’s humanitarian ideals, fair consideration to those who come to Canada claiming persecution;

label: (d)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to offer safe haven to persons with a well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership in a particular social group, as well as those at risk of torture or cruel and unusual treatment or punishment;

label: (e)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to establish fair and efficient procedures that will maintain the integrity of the Canadian refugee protection system, while upholding Canada’s respect for the human rights and fundamental freedoms of all human beings;

label: (f)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to support the self-sufficiency and the social and economic well-being of refugees by facilitating reunification with their family members in Canada;

label: (g)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to protect the health and safety of Canadians and to maintain the security of Canadian society; and

label: (h)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: to promote international justice and security by denying access to Canadian territory to persons, including refugee claimants, who are security risks or serious criminals.

heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: This Act is to be construed and applied in a manner that

label: (a)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: furthers the domestic and international interests of Canada;

label: (b)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: promotes accountability and transparency by enhancing public awareness of immigration and refugee programs;

label: (c)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: facilitates cooperation between the Government of Canada, provincial governments, foreign states, international organizations and non-governmental organizations;

label: (d)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: ensures that decisions taken under this Act are consistent with the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms , including its principles of equality and freedom from discrimination and of the equality of English and French as the official languages of Canada;

label: (e)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: supports the commitment of the Government of Canada to enhance the vitality of the English and French linguistic minority communities in Canada; and

label: (f)
heading_path: Objectives and Application
own_text: complies with international human rights instruments to which Canada is signatory.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
Enabling Authority
own_text: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration is responsible for the administration of this Act.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: The Governor in Council may, by order, designate a minister of the Crown as the Minister responsible for all matters under this Act relating to special advocates. If none is designated, the Minister of Justice is responsible for those matters.

marginal_note: Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: The Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness is responsible for the administration of this Act as it relates to

label: (a)
marginal_note: Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: examinations at ports of entry;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: the enforcement of this Act, including arrest, detention and removal;

label: (c)
marginal_note: Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: the establishment of policies respecting the enforcement of this Act and inadmissibility on grounds of security, violating human or international rights, sanctions, transborder criminality or organized criminality; or

label: (d)
marginal_note: Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: declarations referred to in section 42.1.

marginal_note: Minister of Employment and Social Development
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: In making regulations under paragraphs 32(d.1) to (d.4), the Governor in Council may confer powers and duties on the Minister of Employment and Social Development.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: Subject to subsections (1) to (2), the Governor in Council may, by order,

label: (a)
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: specify which Minister referred to in any of subsections (1) to (2) is the Minister for the purposes of any provision of this Act; and

label: (b)
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: specify that more than one Minister may be the Minister for the purposes of any provision of this Act and specify the circumstances under which each Minister is the Minister.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: Any order made under subsection (3) must be published in Part II of the Canada Gazette .

heading_path: Enabling Authority
Enabling Authority
own_text: Except as otherwise provided, the Governor in Council may make any regulation that is referred to in this Act or that prescribes any matter whose prescription is referred to in this Act.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: Regulations made under this Act that apply in respect of sponsorship applications or applications for permanent or temporary resident visas, permanent or temporary resident status or work or study permits may, if they so provide, apply in respect of any such applications that are pending on the day on which the regulations are made, other than

label: (a)
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: applications to become a permanent resident made in Canada by protected persons; and

label: (b)
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: applications for permanent resident visas made by persons referred to in subsection 99(2) and sponsorship applications made in respect of those applications.

marginal_note: Tabling and referral of proposed regulations
heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: The Minister shall cause a copy of each proposed regulation made under sections 17, 32, 53, 61, 87.2, 102, 116, 150 and 150.1 to be laid before each House of Parliament, and each House shall refer the proposed regulation to the appropriate Committee of that House.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: A proposed regulation that has been laid before each House of Parliament under subsection (2) does not need to be so laid again, whether or not it has been altered.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: The Governor in Council may make the regulation at any time after the proposed regulation has been laid before each House of Parliament under subsection (2).

heading_path: Enabling Authority
Enabling Authority
own_text: The Minister may designate any persons or class of persons as officers to carry out any purpose of any provision of this Act, and shall specify the powers and duties of the officers so designated.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: Anything that may be done by the Minister under this Act may be done by a person that the Minister authorizes in writing, without proof of the authenticity of the authorization.

heading_path: Enabling Authority
own_text: Despite subsection (2), the Minister may not delegate the power conferred by subsection 20.1(1), section 22.1 or subsection 42.1(1) or (2) or 77(1).

heading_path: Agreements
own_text: The Minister, with the approval of the Governor in Council, may enter into an agreement with the government of a foreign state or with an international organization for the purposes of this Act.

heading_path: Agreements
Agreements
own_text: The Minister, with the approval of the Governor in Council, may enter into an agreement with the government of any province for the purposes of this Act. The Minister must publish, once a year, a list of the federal-provincial agreements that are in force.

heading_path: Agreements
own_text: Subject to subsection (3) but despite the other provisions of this Act, the following must be consistent with the federal-provincial agreements:

label: (a)
heading_path: Agreements
own_text: the selection and sponsorship of, and the acquisition of status by, foreign nationals under this Act; and

label: (b)
heading_path: Agreements
own_text: regulations governing those matters, including regulations respecting the examination in Canada of applications to become a permanent resident, or respecting the foreign nationals who may be selected on the basis of an investment in Canada.

heading_path: Agreements
own_text: Subsection (2) is not to be interpreted as limiting the application of any provision of this Act concerning inadmissibility to Canada.

heading_path: Agreements
Agreements
own_text: Where a province has, under a federal-provincial agreement, sole responsibility for the selection of a foreign national who intends to reside in that province as a permanent resident, the following provisions apply to that foreign national, unless the agreement provides otherwise:

label: (a)
heading_path: Agreements
own_text: the foreign national, unless inadmissible under this Act, shall be granted permanent resident status if the foreign national meets the province’s selection criteria;

label: (b)
heading_path: Agreements
own_text: the foreign national shall not be granted permanent resident status if the foreign national does not meet the province’s selection criteria;

label: (c)
heading_path: Agreements
own_text: the foreign national shall not be granted permanent resident status contrary to the provisions of the law of the province governing the number of foreign nationals who may settle in the province as permanent residents, whether that number is an estimate or a maximum, or governing the distribution of that number among classes of foreign nationals; and

label: (d)
heading_path: Agreements
own_text: conditions imposed in accordance with the law of the province have the same force and effect as if they were made under this Act, if they are imposed on a foreign national on or before the grant of permanent resident status.

heading_path: Agreements
own_text: If a federal-provincial agreement gives a province sole responsibility to establish and apply financial criteria with respect to undertakings that sponsors living in that province may make in respect of a foreign national who applies to become a permanent resident, then, unless the agreement provides otherwise, the existence of a right of appeal under the law of that province respecting rejections by provincial officials of applications for sponsorship, for reasons of failing to meet financial criteria or failing to comply with a prior undertaking, prevents the sponsor, except on humanitarian and compassionate grounds, from appealing under this Act against a refusal, based on those reasons, of a visa or permanent resident status.

heading_path: Agreements
Agreements
own_text: The Minister may consult with the governments of the provinces on immigration and refugee protection policies and programs, in order to facilitate cooperation and to take into consideration the effects that the implementation of this Act may have on the provinces.

heading_path: Agreements
own_text: The Minister must consult with the governments of the provinces respecting the number of foreign nationals in each class who will become permanent residents each year, their distribution in Canada taking into account regional economic and demographic requirements, and the measures to be undertaken to facilitate their integration into Canadian society.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.01 Biometric Information
own_text: A person who makes a claim, application or request under this Act must follow the procedures set out in the regulations for the collection and verification of biometric information, including procedures for the collection of further biometric information for verification purposes after a person’s claim, application or request is allowed or accepted.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.01 Biometric Information
own_text: The regulations may provide for any matter relating to the application of section 10.01 and may include provisions respecting

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.01 Biometric Information
own_text: restrictions on the persons to whom that section applies and on the claims, applications or requests to which it applies;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.01 Biometric Information
own_text: the procedures for the collection and verification of biometric information;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.01 Biometric Information
own_text: the biometric information that is to be collected;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.01 Biometric Information
own_text: the circumstances in which a person is not required to provide certain biometric information;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.01 Biometric Information
own_text: the processing of the collected biometric information, including the creation of biometric templates or the conversion of the information into digital biometric formats; and

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.01 Biometric Information
own_text: the circumstances in which a person is exempt from the application of that section.

marginal_note: Application for permanent residence — invitation to apply
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application

marginal_note: Application for permanent residence — invitation to apply
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: A foreign national who seeks to enter or remain in Canada as a member of a class that is referred to in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(a) may make an application for permanent residence only if the Minister has issued them an invitation to do so, the invitation has not been cancelled under subsection 10.2(5) and the applicable period specified in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(k) has not expired.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: A foreign national who is a member of a portion of the prescribed class of provincial nominees set out in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(a) may be issued an invitation only in respect of that class.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: An instruction may be given under paragraph 10.3(1)(a) only in respect of a class that is part of the economic class referred to in subsection 12(2).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: In the case of the prescribed class of provincial nominees, an instruction may be given under paragraph 10.3(1)(a) in respect of the foreign nationals who are nominated by the government of a particular province in accordance with an agreement referred to in section 8, or in respect of a portion of those foreign nationals.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: A foreign national who wishes to be invited to make an application must submit an expression of interest to the Minister by means of an electronic system in accordance with instructions given under section 10.3 unless the instructions provide that they may do so by other means.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: A foreign national may not submit an expression of interest if they have been determined to be — and continue to be — inadmissible for misrepresentation.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: A foreign national who has submitted an expression of interest may not submit another one before the expiry of the period referred to in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(f).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: A foreign national who is invited to make an application and does not do so within the period specified in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(k) is not eligible to be invited to make an application in relation to the expression of interest on the basis of which the invitation was issued.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: Subsection (6) does not apply to a foreign national who declines an invitation to make an application within the period specified in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(k).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: In processing an expression of interest, the Minister

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: is to determine whether the foreign national is eligible to be invited to make an application by applying the criteria set out in instructions given under paragraph 10.3(1)(e) and is to advise the foreign national of the determination in accordance with instructions given under paragraph 10.3(1)(l); and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: subject to subsection (2), is to determine whether, in accordance with instructions given under paragraph 10.3(1)(i), the foreign national occupies the rank required to be invited to make an application and, if so, is to issue the invitation in accordance with instructions given under paragraph 10.3(1)(l).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: A determination under paragraph (1)(b) may be made only if the number of invitations that have been issued is less than the number provided for in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(j).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: The Minister is to use an electronic system to carry out any applicable instruction given under subsection 10.3(1) and to make a determination under paragraph (1)(a) or (b).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: An expression of interest must be processed in compliance with any applicable instruction.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: The Minister may cancel an invitation to make an application if the invitation was issued in error.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: The Minister may give instructions governing any matter relating to the application of this Division, including instructions respecting

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the classes in respect of which subsection 10.1(1) applies;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the electronic system referred to in subsections 10.1(3) and 10.2(3);

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the submission and processing of an expression of interest, including by means of the electronic system;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the circumstances in which an expression of interest may be submitted by means other than the electronic system and respecting those other means;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the criteria that a foreign national must meet to be eligible to be invited to make an application;

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the period during which a foreign national remains eligible to be invited to make an application;

label: (g)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the personal information that the Minister may disclose under section 10.4 and the entities to which that information may be disclosed;

label: (h)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the basis on which an eligible foreign national may be ranked;

label: (h.1)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: subject to subsection (1.01), the establishment of categories of eligible foreign nationals for the purposes of ranking, which groupings may consist of

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: all eligible foreign nationals,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: eligible foreign nationals who are eligible to be members of a class referred to in an instruction given under paragraph (a), or

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: eligible foreign nationals who are eligible to be members of a category established in an instruction given under paragraph (h.2);

label: (h.2)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the establishment of categories for the purposes of ranking and the criteria for eligibility to be a member of a category;

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the rank within a grouping that an eligible foreign national must occupy to be invited to make an application in respect of a class referred to in an instruction given under paragraph (a);

label: (j)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the number of invitations that may be issued within a specified period in respect of a grouping;

label: (j.1)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the class referred to in an instruction given under paragraph (a) in respect of which an eligible foreign national who is invited to make an application must apply, if the foreign national is eligible to be a member of more than one class;

label: (k)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the period within which an application must be made once an invitation has been issued;

label: (l)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: the means by which a foreign national is to be advised of any matter relating to their expression of interest, including an invitation to make an application; and

label: (m)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: any matter for which a recommendation to the Minister or a decision may or must be made by a designated person, institution or organization with respect to a foreign national.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: An instruction given under paragraph (1)(h.1) must not establish a category in respect of which a public consultation process referred to in subsection 10.5(1) has not been given the opportunity to provide advice and recommendations.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: If the Minister establishes a category in an instruction given under paragraph (1)(h.2), the Minister shall set out, in the instruction, the economic goal that the Minister seeks to support in establishing the category.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: For greater certainty, an instruction given under paragraph (1)(j) may provide that the number of invitations that may be issued in any specified period in respect of a grouping be zero.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: An instruction given under any of paragraphs (1)(a), (b) and (e) to (l) applies in respect of an expression of interest that is submitted before the day on which the instruction takes effect, unless the instruction provides otherwise.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: Instructions given under subsection (1) must be published on the Department of Citizenship and Immigration’s Internet site. Instructions given under any of paragraphs (1)(a), (d) to (g), (k) and (l) must also be published in the Canada Gazette .

marginal_note: Criteria provided for under other Divisions
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: For greater certainty, an instruction given under subsection (1) may provide for criteria that are more stringent than the criteria or requirements provided for in or under any other Division of this Act regarding applications for permanent residence.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: For the purpose of facilitating the selection of a foreign national as a member of the economic class or as a temporary resident, the Minister may disclose to an entity that is referred to in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(g) the personal information referred to in that instruction that is

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: provided to the Minister by the foreign national under section 10.1 or by a third party for the purposes of section 10.1 or 10.2; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: created by the Minister, on the basis of the information referred to in paragraph (a), for the purposes of sections 10.1 to 10.3.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: For the purpose of establishing categories of eligible foreign nationals under subparagraph 10.3(1)(h.1)(iii), the Minister must engage in a public consultation process with stakeholders, including provinces and territories, industry, unions, employers, workers, worker advocacy groups, settlement provider organizations and immigration researchers and practitioners, to obtain information, advice and recommendations in respect of the labour market conditions, including occupations expected to face shortage conditions, as well as on how categories can be formed to meet economic goals.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: The advice and recommendations from the public consultation process must be based on written submissions provided by relevant industry members and stakeholders.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: The Minister shall cause to be tabled before each House of Parliament, not later than the fifth sitting day of that House after January 31 following the end of each fiscal year, a report containing the list of the categories of eligible foreign nationals established in an instruction made under paragraph 10.3(1)(h.1) and the selection criteria and the process applied for the establishment of those categories.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 0.1 Invitation to Make an Application
own_text: After it is tabled, the report stands referred to the committee of the Senate, the House of Commons or both Houses of Parliament that may be designated or established for the purpose of reviewing the report.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: A foreign national must, before entering Canada, apply to an officer for a visa or for any other document required by the regulations. The visa or document may be issued if, following an examination, the officer is satisfied that the foreign national is not inadmissible and meets the requirements of this Act.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: Despite subsection (1), a foreign national must, before entering Canada, apply for an electronic travel authorization required by the regulations by means of an electronic system, unless the regulations provide that the application may be made by other means. The application may be examined by an officer and, if the officer determines that the foreign national is not inadmissible and meets the requirements of this Act, the authorization may be issued by the officer.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: A designated foreign national may not make an application for permanent residence under subsection (1)

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: if they have made a claim for refugee protection but have not made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the claim is made;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: if they have made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the application is made; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: in any other case, until five years after the day on which they become a designated foreign national.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: The processing of an application for permanent residence under subsection (1) of a foreign national who, after the application is made, becomes a designated foreign national is suspended

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: if the foreign national has made a claim for refugee protection but has not made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the claim is made;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: if the foreign national has made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the application is made; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: in any other case, until five years after the day on which the foreign national becomes a designated foreign national.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: The officer may refuse to consider an application for permanent residence made under subsection (1) if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: the designated foreign national fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with any condition imposed on them under subsection 58(4) or section 58.1 or any requirement imposed on them under section 98.1; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: less than 12 months have passed since the end of the applicable period referred to in subsection (1.1) or (1.2).

marginal_note: If sponsor does not meet requirements
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: The officer may not issue a visa or other document to a foreign national whose sponsor does not meet the sponsorship requirements of this Act.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements

marginal_note: Visa or other document not to be issued
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements

marginal_note: Visa or other document not to be issued
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: An officer may not issue a visa or other document in respect of an application for permanent residence to a foreign national who was issued an invitation under Division 0.1 to make that application if — at the time the invitation was issued or at the time the officer received their application — the foreign national

label: (a)
marginal_note: Visa or other document not to be issued
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: did not meet the criteria set out in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(e);

label: (b)
marginal_note: Visa or other document not to be issued
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: did not have the qualifications on the basis of which they were ranked under an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(h) and were issued the invitation; or

label: (c)
marginal_note: Visa or other document not to be issued
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: did not meet the criteria for membership in a category that was established in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(h.2), if they were issued an invitation on the basis that they were eligible to be a member of that category.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: Despite subsection (1), an officer may issue the visa or other document if, at the time the officer received their application,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: the foreign national did not meet the criteria set out in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(e) — or they did not have the qualifications on the basis of which they were ranked under an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(h) or did not meet the criteria for membership in a category that was established in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(h.2) — because the foreign national’s birthday occurred after the invitation was issued; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: the foreign national did not have the qualifications they had at the time the invitation was issued and on the basis of which they were ranked under an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(h), but

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: they met the criteria set out in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(e),

label: (i.1)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: they met the criteria for membership of a category established in an instruction given under paragraph 10.3(1)(h.2), if they were issued the invitation on the basis that they were eligible to be a member of that category, and

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: they occupied a rank that is not lower than the rank that a foreign national was required to have occupied to be invited to make an application.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Requirements
own_text: An officer may terminate the processing of an application for a visa or other document in the prescribed circumstances.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Selection of Permanent Residents
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Selection of Permanent Residents
own_text: A foreign national may be selected as a member of the family class on the basis of their relationship as the spouse, common-law partner, child, parent or other prescribed family member of a Canadian citizen or permanent resident.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Selection of Permanent Residents
own_text: A foreign national may be selected as a member of the economic class on the basis of their ability to become economically established in Canada.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Selection of Permanent Residents
own_text: A foreign national, inside or outside Canada, may be selected as a person who under this Act is a Convention refugee or as a person in similar circumstances, taking into account Canada’s humanitarian tradition with respect to the displaced and the persecuted.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Sponsorship of Foreign Nationals
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Sponsorship of Foreign Nationals
own_text: A Canadian citizen or permanent resident, or a group of Canadian citizens or permanent residents, a corporation incorporated under a law of Canada or of a province or an unincorporated organization or association under federal or provincial law — or any combination of them — may sponsor a foreign national, subject to the regulations.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Sponsorship of Foreign Nationals
own_text: [Repealed, 2012, c. 17, s. 7]

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Sponsorship of Foreign Nationals
own_text: [Repealed, 2012, c. 17, s. 7]

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Sponsorship of Foreign Nationals
own_text: An officer shall apply the regulations on sponsorship referred to in paragraph 14(2)(e) in accordance with any instructions that the Minister may make.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Undertakings
own_text: An undertaking given under this Act in respect of a foreign national — including a sponsorship undertaking — is binding on the person who gives it.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Undertakings
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Undertakings
own_text: If required to do so by the regulations, a foreign national who makes an application for a visa or for permanent or temporary resident status must obtain the undertaking specified in the regulations.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Undertakings
own_text: An officer must apply the regulations made under paragraph 14(2)(e.1) in accordance with any instructions that the Minister may give.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: The regulations may provide for any matter relating to the application of this Division, and may define, for the purposes of this Act, the terms used in this Division.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: The regulations may prescribe, and govern any matter relating to, classes of permanent residents or foreign nationals, including the classes referred to in section 12, and may include provisions respecting

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: selection criteria, the weight, if any, to be given to all or some of those criteria, the procedures to be followed in evaluating all or some of those criteria and the circumstances in which an officer may substitute for those criteria their evaluation of the likelihood of a foreign national’s ability to become economically established in Canada;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: applications for visas and other documents and their issuance or refusal, with respect to foreign nationals and their family members;

label: (b.1)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: the circumstances in which an officer may terminate the processing of an application for a visa or other document;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: the number of applications that may be processed or approved in a year, the number of visas and other documents that may be issued in a year, and the measures to be taken when that number is exceeded;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: conditions that may or must be imposed, varied or cancelled, individually or by class, on permanent residents and foreign nationals;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: sponsorships;

label: (e.1)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: undertakings, and penalties for failure to comply with undertakings;

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: deposits or guarantees of the performance of obligations under this Act that are to be given by any person to the Minister;

label: (f.1)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: the power to inspect, including the power to require documents to be provided for inspection, for the purpose of verifying compliance with undertakings; and

label: (g)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
own_text: any matter for which a recommendation to the Minister or a decision may or must be made by a designated person, institution or organization with respect to a foreign national or sponsor.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Regulations
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: For the purpose of supporting the attainment of economic goals established by the Government of Canada, the Minister may give instructions establishing a class of permanent residents as part of the economic class referred to in subsection 12(2) and, in respect of the class that is established, governing any matter referred to in paragraphs 14(2)(a) to (g), 26(a), (b), (d) and (e) and 32(d) and the fees for processing applications for permanent resident visas or for permanent resident status and providing for cases in which those fees may be waived.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: Despite any instruction given by the Minister under paragraph 87.3(3)(c), no more than 2,750 applications in a class established under subsection (1) may be processed in any year.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: Subject to subsection (4), regulations that apply to all classes prescribed under subsection 14(2) that are part of the economic class referred to in subsection 12(2) apply to a class established under subsection (1).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: The Minister may specify in an instruction that regulations made under subsection 14(2), paragraph 26(a), (b), (d) or (e) or 32(d) or subsection 89(1) do not apply to a class established under subsection (1).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: For greater certainty, regulations that apply to only one class prescribed under subsection 14(2) that is part of the economic class referred to in subsection 12(2) — or to only certain classes that are part of that economic class — do not apply to a class established under subsection (1). However, an instruction given under that subsection may specify otherwise.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: The instructions do not apply in respect of a prescribed class.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: An officer must comply with the instructions before processing an application and when processing one.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: An instruction that amends another instruction may, if it so provides, apply in respect of applications in a class established by the original instruction that are pending on the day on which the amending instruction takes effect.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: An instruction given under subsection (1) has effect for the period specified in the instruction, which is not to exceed five years starting on the day on which the instruction first takes effect. No amendment to or renewal of an instruction may extend the five-year period.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: Despite subsection (9), the Minister may direct officers to process, after the end of the effective period of an instruction, applications in a class established by the instruction that were made during the period in which the instruction had effect.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: The Service Fees Act does not apply in respect of the fees referred to in subsection (1).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 1 Requirements and Selection > Minister’s Instructions
own_text: Instructions must be published in the Canada Gazette .

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: An officer is authorized to proceed with an examination if a person makes an application to the officer in accordance with this Act or if an application is made under subsection 11(1.01).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: In the case of a foreign national referred to in subsection 9(1), an examination of whether the foreign national complies with the applicable selection criteria shall be conducted solely on the basis of documents delivered by the province indicating that the competent authority of the province is of the opinion that the foreign national complies with the province’s selection criteria.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: An officer may board and inspect any means of transportation bringing persons to Canada, examine any person carried by that means of transportation and any record or document respecting that person, seize and remove the record or document to obtain copies or extracts and hold the means of transportation until the inspection and examination are completed.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: The officer shall conduct the examination in accordance with any instructions that the Minister may give.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: A health insurance policy purchased from an insurance company outside Canada that is approved by the Minister satisfies any requirement in an instruction given under subsection 15(4) that a foreign national who applies for a temporary resident visa in order to visit their Canadian citizen or permanent resident child or grandchild for an extended period must have private health insurance.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: A person who makes an application must answer truthfully all questions put to them for the purpose of the examination and must produce a visa and all relevant evidence and documents that the officer reasonably requires.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: A person who makes an application must, on request of an officer, appear for an examination.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: In the case of a foreign national,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: the relevant evidence referred to in subsection (1) includes photographic and fingerprint evidence; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: subject to the regulations, the foreign national must submit to a medical examination.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: A foreign national who makes an application must, on request of an officer, appear for an interview for the purpose of an investigation conducted by the Canadian Security Intelligence Service under section 15 of the Canadian Security Intelligence Service Act for the purpose of providing advice or information to the Minister under section 14 of that Act and must answer truthfully all questions put to them during the interview.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: An officer may require or obtain from a permanent resident or a foreign national who is arrested, detained, subject to an examination or subject to a removal order, any evidence — photographic, fingerprint or otherwise — that may be used to establish their identity or compliance with this Act.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 2 Examination
own_text: The regulations may provide for any matter relating to the application of this Division, and may include provisions respecting the conduct of examinations.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: Subject to the regulations, every person seeking to enter Canada must appear for an examination to determine whether that person has a right to enter Canada or is or may become authorized to enter and remain in Canada.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: Subsection (1) also applies to persons who, without leaving Canada, seek to leave an area at an airport that is reserved for passengers who are in transit or who are waiting to depart Canada.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: Even though a person seeking to enter Canada is not, in accordance with regulations made under subsection 26(2), required to appear for an examination, an officer may require the person to do so.

marginal_note: Right of entry of citizens and Indians
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining

marginal_note: Right of entry of citizens and Indians
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: Every Canadian citizen within the meaning of the Citizenship Act and every person registered as an Indian under the Indian Act has the right to enter and remain in Canada in accordance with this Act, and an officer shall allow the person to enter Canada if satisfied following an examination on their entry that the person is a citizen or registered Indian.

marginal_note: Right of entry of permanent residents
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: An officer shall allow a permanent resident to enter Canada if satisfied following an examination on their entry that they have that status.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: Every foreign national, other than a foreign national referred to in section 19, who seeks to enter or remain in Canada must establish,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: to become a permanent resident, that they hold the visa or other document required under the regulations and have come to Canada in order to establish permanent residence; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: to become a temporary resident, that they hold the visa or other document required under the regulations and will leave Canada by the end of the period authorized for their stay.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: A foreign national who is the subject of a declaration made under subsection 22.1(1) must not seek to enter or remain in Canada as a temporary resident.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: A foreign national referred to in subsection 9(1) must also establish, to become a permanent resident, that they hold a document issued by the province indicating that the competent authority of the province is of the opinion that the foreign national complies with the province’s selection criteria.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: An officer may, in the prescribed circumstances, cancel, suspend or vary a visa or other document.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: For greater certainty, subsection (1) does not affect any other lawful authority to cancel, suspend or vary a visa or other document.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: For greater certainty, the authority to vary under subsection (1) does not include the authority to grant permanent resident status.

marginal_note: Designation — human smuggling or other irregular arrival
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining

marginal_note: Designation — human smuggling or other irregular arrival
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: The Minister may, by order, having regard to the public interest, designate as an irregular arrival the arrival in Canada of a group of persons if he or she

label: (a)
marginal_note: Designation — human smuggling or other irregular arrival
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: is of the opinion that examinations of the persons in the group, particularly for the purpose of establishing identity or determining inadmissibility — and any investigations concerning persons in the group — cannot be conducted in a timely manner; or

label: (b)
marginal_note: Designation — human smuggling or other irregular arrival
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: has reasonable grounds to suspect that, in relation to the arrival in Canada of the group, there has been, or will be, a contravention of subsection 117(1) for profit, or for the benefit of, at the direction of or in association with a criminal organization or terrorist group.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: When a designation is made under subsection (1), a foreign national — other than a foreign national referred to in section 19 — who is part of the group whose arrival is the subject of the designation becomes a designated foreign national unless, on arrival, they hold the visa or other document required under the regulations and, on examination, the officer is satisfied that they are not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: An order made under subsection (1) is not a statutory instrument for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act . However, it must be published in the Canada Gazette .

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: A designated foreign national may not apply to become a permanent resident

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: if they have made a claim for refugee protection but have not made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the claim is made;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: if they have made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the application is made; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: in any other case, until five years after the day on which they become a designated foreign national.

marginal_note: Suspension of application for permanent residence
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: The processing of an application for permanent residence of a foreign national who, after the application is made, becomes a designated foreign national is suspended

label: (a)
marginal_note: Suspension of application for permanent residence
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: if the foreign national has made a claim for refugee protection but has not made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the claim is made;

label: (b)
marginal_note: Suspension of application for permanent residence
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: if the foreign national has made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the application is made; or

label: (c)
marginal_note: Suspension of application for permanent residence
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: in any other case, until five years after the day on which the foreign national becomes a designated foreign national.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: The officer may refuse to consider an application for permanent residence if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: the designated foreign national fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with any condition imposed on them under subsection 58(4) or section 58.1 or any requirement imposed on them under section 98.1; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Entering and Remaining
own_text: less than 12 months have passed since the end of the applicable period referred to in subsection (1) or (2).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A foreign national becomes a permanent resident if an officer is satisfied that the foreign national has applied for that status, has met the obligations set out in paragraph 20(1)(a) and subsection 20(2) and is not inadmissible.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: Except in the case of a person described in subsection 112(3) or a person who is a member of a prescribed class of persons, a person whose application for protection has been finally determined by the Board to be a Convention refugee or to be a person in need of protection, or a person whose application for protection has been allowed by the Minister, becomes, subject to any federal-provincial agreement referred to in subsection 9(1), a permanent resident if the officer is satisfied that they have made their application in accordance with the regulations and that they are not inadmissible on any ground referred to in section 34, 35 or 35.1, subsection 36(1) or section 37 or 38.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A person in respect of whom the Minister has made an application under subsection 108(2) may not become a permanent resident under subsection (2) while the application is pending.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A foreign national becomes a temporary resident if an officer is satisfied that the foreign national has applied for that status, has met the obligations set out in paragraph 20(1)(b), is not inadmissible and is not the subject of a declaration made under subsection 22.1(1).

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: An intention by a foreign national to become a permanent resident does not preclude them from becoming a temporary resident if the officer is satisfied that they will leave Canada by the end of the period authorized for their stay.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: The Minister may, on the Minister’s own initiative, declare that a foreign national, other than a foreign national referred to in section 19, may not become a temporary resident if the Minister is of the opinion that it is justified by public policy considerations.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A declaration has effect for the period specified by the Minister, which is not to exceed 36 months.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: The Minister may, at any time, revoke a declaration or shorten its effective period.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: The report required under section 94 must include the number of declarations made under subsection (1) and set out the public policy considerations that led to the making of the declarations.

marginal_note: Entry to complete examination or hearing
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: An officer may authorize a person to enter Canada for the purpose of further examination or an admissibility hearing under this Part.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A foreign national who, in the opinion of an officer, is inadmissible or does not meet the requirements of this Act becomes a temporary resident if an officer is of the opinion that it is justified in the circumstances and issues a temporary resident permit, which may be cancelled at any time.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A foreign national referred to in subsection (1) to whom an officer issues a temporary resident permit outside Canada does not become a temporary resident until they have been examined upon arrival in Canada.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: In applying subsection (1), the officer shall act in accordance with any instructions that the Minister may make.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A foreign national whose claim for refugee protection has been determined to be ineligible to be referred to the Refugee Protection Division may not request a temporary resident permit if they have made an application for protection to the Minister that is pending.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A foreign national whose claim for refugee protection has not been allowed may not request a temporary resident permit if less than 12 months have passed since

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: the day on which their claim was rejected or determined to be withdrawn or abandoned by the Refugee Protection Division, in the case where no appeal was made and no application was made to the Federal Court for leave to commence an application for judicial review; or

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: in any other case, the latest of

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: the day on which their claim was rejected or determined to be withdrawn or abandoned by the Refugee Protection Division or, if there was more than one such rejection or determination, the day on which the last one occurred,

label: (ii)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: the day on which their claim was rejected or determined to be withdrawn or abandoned by the Refugee Appeal Division or, if there was more than one such rejection or determination, the day on which the last one occurred, and

label: (iii)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: the day on which the Federal Court refused their application for leave to commence an application for judicial review, or denied their application for judicial review, with respect to their claim.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A designated foreign national may not request a temporary resident permit

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: if they have made a claim for refugee protection but have not made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the claim is made;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: if they have made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the application is made; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: in any other case, until five years after the day on which the foreign national becomes a designated foreign national.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: The processing of a request for a temporary resident permit of a foreign national who, after the request is made, becomes a designated foreign national is suspended

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: if the foreign national has made a claim for refugee protection but has not made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the claim is made;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: if the foreign national has made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the application is made; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: in any other case, until five years after the day on which the foreign national becomes a designated foreign national.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: The officer may refuse to consider a request for a temporary resident permit if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: the designated foreign national fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with any condition imposed on them under subsection 58(4) or section 58.1 or any requirement imposed on them under section 98.1; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: less than 12 months have passed since the end of the applicable period referred to in subsection (5) or (6).

marginal_note: Humanitarian and compassionate considerations — request of foreign national
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter

marginal_note: Humanitarian and compassionate considerations — request of foreign national
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: Subject to subsection (1.2), the Minister must, on request of a foreign national in Canada who applies for permanent resident status and who is inadmissible — other than under section 34, 35, 35.1 or 37 — or who does not meet the requirements of this Act, and may, on request of a foreign national outside Canada — other than a foreign national who is inadmissible under section 34, 35, 35.1 or 37 — who applies for a permanent resident visa, examine the circumstances concerning the foreign national and may grant the foreign national permanent resident status or an exemption from any applicable criteria or obligations of this Act if the Minister is of the opinion that it is justified by humanitarian and compassionate considerations relating to the foreign national, taking into account the best interests of a child directly affected.

heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: A designated foreign national may not make a request under subsection (1)

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
own_text: if they have made a claim for refugee protection but have not made an application for protection, until five years after the day on which a final determination in respect of the claim is made;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 1 Immigration to Canada > DIVISION 3 Entering and Remaining in Canada > Status and Authorization to Enter
