own_text: despite paragraph (e), the representative or agent may not observe any part of the proceedings that deals with information or other evidence in respect of which an application has been made under section 86, and not rejected, or with information or other evidence protected under that section.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: A person who is the subject of proceedings before any Division of the Board and the Minister may, at their own expense, be represented by legal or other counsel.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: If a person who is the subject of proceedings is under 18 years of age or unable, in the opinion of the applicable Division, to appreciate the nature of the proceedings, the Division shall designate a person to represent the person.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: A Division may determine that a proceeding before it has been abandoned if the Division is of the opinion that the applicant is in default in the proceedings, including by failing to appear for a hearing, to provide information required by the Division or to communicate with the Division on being requested to do so.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: For greater certainty, if the Refugee Protection Division or the Refugee Appeal Division is prevented under section 104.1 from considering a claim or appeal, it may determine under subsection (1) that the claim or appeal has been abandoned.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: A Division may refuse to allow an applicant to withdraw from a proceeding if it is of the opinion that the withdrawal would be an abuse of process under its rules.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: In the case of a decision of a Division, other than an interlocutory decision:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: the decision takes effect in accordance with the rules;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: reasons for the decision must be given;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: the decision may be rendered orally or in writing, except a decision of the Refugee Appeal Division, which must be rendered in writing;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: if the Refugee Protection Division rejects a claim, written reasons must be provided to the claimant and the Minister;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: written reasons for the decision must be provided to the person who is the subject of the decision and to the Minister in circumstances provided for in the rules of the Board or if the person or the Minister requests them within 10 days after notice of the decision is provided; and

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Provisions that Apply to All Divisions
own_text: the period in which to apply for judicial review with respect to a decision of the Board is calculated from the giving of notice of the decision or from the sending of written reasons, whichever is later.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: The Refugee Protection Division consists of the Deputy Chairperson, Assistant Deputy Chairpersons and other members, including coordinating members, necessary to carry out its functions.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: The members of the Refugee Protection Division are appointed in accordance with the Public Service Employment Act .

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: The Refugee Protection Division, in any proceeding before it,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: may inquire into any matter that it considers relevant to establishing whether a claim is well-founded;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: must hold a hearing;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: must notify the person who is the subject of the proceeding and the Minister of the hearing;

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: must provide the Minister, on request, with the documents and information referred to in subsection 100(4);

label: (d.1)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: may question the witnesses, including the person who is the subject of the proceeding;

label: (e)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: must give the person and the Minister a reasonable opportunity to present evidence, question witnesses and make representations;

label: (f)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: may, despite paragraph (b), allow a claim for refugee protection without a hearing, if the Minister has not notified the Division, within the period set out in the rules of the Board, of the Minister’s intention to intervene;

label: (g)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: is not bound by any legal or technical rules of evidence;

label: (h)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: may receive and base a decision on evidence that is adduced in the proceedings and considered credible or trustworthy in the circumstances; and

label: (i)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: may take notice of any facts that may be judicially noticed, any other generally recognized facts and any information or opinion that is within its specialized knowledge.

marginal_note: No reopening of claim or application
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Protection Division
own_text: The Refugee Protection Division does not have jurisdiction to reopen on any ground — including a failure to observe a principle of natural justice — a claim for refugee protection, an application for protection or an application for cessation or vacation, in respect of which the Refugee Appeal Division or the Federal Court, as the case may be, has made a final determination.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: In the case of a proceeding of the Refugee Appeal Division,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: the Division must give notice of any hearing to the Minister and to the person who is the subject of the appeal;

label: (a.1)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: subject to subsection 110(4), if a hearing is held, the Division must give the person who is the subject of the appeal and the Minister the opportunity to present evidence, question witnesses and make submissions;

label: (a.2)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: the Division is not bound by any legal or technical rules of evidence;

label: (a.3)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: the Division may receive and base a decision on evidence that is adduced in the proceedings and considered credible or trustworthy in the circumstances;

label: (a.4)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: the Minister may, at any time before the Division makes a decision, after giving notice to the Division and to the person who is the subject of the appeal, intervene in the appeal;

label: (a.5)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: the Minister may, at any time before the Division makes a decision, submit documentary evidence and make written submissions in support of the Minister’s appeal or intervention in the appeal;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: the Division may take notice of any facts that may be judicially noticed and of any other generally recognized facts and any information or opinion that is within its specialized knowledge; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: a decision of a panel of three members of the Refugee Appeal Division has, for the Refugee Protection Division and for a panel of one member of the Refugee Appeal Division, the same precedential value as a decision of an appeal court has for a trial court.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Refugee Appeal Division
own_text: The Refugee Appeal Division does not have jurisdiction to reopen on any ground — including a failure to observe a principle of natural justice — an appeal in respect of which the Federal Court has made a final determination.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Division
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Division
own_text: The Immigration Division consists of the Deputy Chairperson, Assistant Deputy Chairpersons and other members necessary to carry out its functions.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Division
own_text: The members of the Immigration Division are appointed in accordance with the Public Service Employment Act .

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Division
own_text: The Immigration Division, in any proceeding before it,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Division
own_text: must, where practicable, hold a hearing;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Division
own_text: must give notice of the proceeding to the Minister and to the person who is the subject of the proceeding and hear the matter without delay;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Division
own_text: is not bound by any legal or technical rules of evidence; and

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Division
own_text: may receive and base a decision on evidence adduced in the proceedings that it considers credible or trustworthy in the circumstances.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
own_text: The Immigration Appeal Division is a court of record and shall have an official seal, which shall be judicially noticed.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
own_text: The Immigration Appeal Division has all the powers, rights and privileges vested in a superior court of record with respect to any matter necessary for the exercise of its jurisdiction, including the swearing and examination of witnesses, the production and inspection of documents and the enforcement of its orders.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
own_text: The Immigration Appeal Division, in any proceeding before it,

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
own_text: must, in the case of an appeal under subsection 63(4), hold a hearing;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
own_text: is not bound by any legal or technical rules of evidence; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
own_text: may receive and base a decision on evidence adduced in the proceedings that it considers credible or trustworthy in the circumstances.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Immigration Appeal Division
own_text: In the case of an appeal by a permanent resident under subsection 63(4), the Immigration Appeal Division may, after considering submissions from the Minister and the permanent resident and if satisfied that the presence of the permanent resident at the hearing is necessary, order the permanent resident to physically appear at the hearing, in which case an officer shall issue a travel document for that purpose.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: The Chairperson may request the Minister to decide whether any member of the Immigration Appeal Division or the Refugee Appeal Division should be subject to remedial or disciplinary measures for a reason set out in subsection (2).

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: The request is to be based on the reason that the member has become incapacitated from the proper execution of that office by reason of infirmity, has been guilty of misconduct, has failed in the proper execution of that office or has been placed, by conduct or otherwise, in a position that is incompatible with due execution of that office.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: On receipt of the request, the Minister may take one or more of the following measures:

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: obtain, in an informal and expeditious manner, any information that the Minister considers necessary;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: refer the matter for mediation, if the Minister is satisfied that the issues in relation to the request may be appropriately resolved by mediation;

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: request of the Governor in Council that an inquiry be held under section 178; or

label: (d)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: advise the Chairperson that the Minister considers that it is not necessary to take further measures under this section or sections 178 to 185.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: On receipt of a request referred to in paragraph 177(c), the Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Justice, appoint a judge of a superior court to conduct an inquiry.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: The judge has all the powers, rights and privileges that are vested in a superior court, including the power

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: to issue a summons requiring any person to appear at the time and place mentioned in the summons to testify about all matters within that person’s knowledge relative to the inquiry and to produce any document or thing relative to the inquiry that the person has or controls; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: to administer oaths and examine any person on oath.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: The judge may engage the services of counsel and other persons having technical or specialized knowledge to assist the judge in conducting the inquiry, establish the terms and conditions of their engagement and, with the approval of the Treasury Board, fix and pay their remuneration and expenses.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: An inquiry must be held in public. However, the judge may, on application, take any appropriate measures and make any order that the judge considers necessary to ensure the confidentiality of the inquiry if, after having considered all available alternate measures, the judge is satisfied that there is

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: a real and substantial risk that matters involving public security will be disclosed;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: a real and substantial risk to the fairness of the inquiry such that the need to prevent disclosure outweighs the societal interest that the inquiry be conducted in public; or

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: a serious possibility that the life, liberty or security of a person will be endangered.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: If the judge considers it appropriate, the judge may take any measures and make any order that the judge considers necessary to ensure the confidentiality of a hearing held in respect of an application under subsection (1).

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: In conducting an inquiry, the judge is not bound by any legal or technical rules of evidence and may receive, and base a decision on, evidence presented in the proceedings that the judge considers credible or trustworthy in the circumstances of the case.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: An interested party may, with leave of the judge, intervene in an inquiry on any terms and conditions that the judge considers appropriate.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: The member who is the subject of the inquiry shall be given reasonable notice of the subject-matter of the inquiry and of the time and place of any hearing and shall be given an opportunity, in person or by counsel, to be heard at the hearing, to cross-examine witnesses and to present evidence.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: After an inquiry has been completed, the judge must submit a report containing the judge’s findings and recommendations, if any, to the Minister.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: The judge may, for any of the reasons set out in subsection 176(2), recommend in the report that the member be suspended without pay or removed from office or that any other disciplinary measure or any remedial measure be taken.

marginal_note: Transmission of report to Governor in Council
heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: If the Minister receives a report of an inquiry in which the judge makes a recommendation, the Minister shall send the report to the Governor in Council who may, if the Governor in Council considers it appropriate, suspend the member without pay, remove the member from office or impose any other disciplinary measure or any remedial measure.

heading_path: PART 4 Immigration and Refugee Board > Remedial and Disciplinary Measures
own_text: Nothing in sections 176 to 185 affects any right or power of the Governor in Council in relation to the removal of a member from office for cause.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: The Minister may administer this Act using electronic means, including as it relates to its enforcement.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: This Part does not apply to the Minister of Employment and Social Development in respect of any activity the administration of which is the responsibility of that Minister under this Act.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: For greater certainty, any person or class of persons who are designated as officers by the Minister to carry out any purpose of this Act may, in the exercise of their powers or the performance of their duties and functions, use the electronic means that are made available or specified by the Minister.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: For greater certainty, a person who has been authorized by the Minister to do anything that may be done by the Minister under this Act, may do so using the electronic means that are made available or specified by the Minister.

marginal_note: Decision, determination or examination by automated system
heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: For greater certainty, an electronic system, including an automated system, may be used by the Minister to make a decision or determination under this Act, or by an officer to make a decision or determination or to proceed with an examination under this Act, if the system is made available to the officer by the Minister.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: A requirement under this Act to provide a signature, or to make an application, request, claim, decision or determination, or to submit or issue any document, or to give notice or provide information, or to submit a document in its original form, is satisfied by its electronic version, if

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: the electronic version is provided by the electronic means, including an electronic system, that are made available or specified by the Minister; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: any other requirements that may be prescribed have been met.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: The regulations may provide for any matter respecting the application of section 186.1 and paragraph 186.2(b), and may include provisions respecting

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: the technology or format to be used, or the standards, specifications or processes to be followed, including for the making or verifying of an electronic signature and the manner in which it is to be used; and

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: the date and time when, and the place where, an electronic version of an application, request, claim, notice, decision, determination, document or any information is deemed to be sent or received.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: The regulations may require a foreign national or another individual who, or entity that, makes an application, request or claim, submits any document or provides information under this Act to do so using electronic means, including an electronic system. The regulations may also include provisions respecting those means, including that system, respecting the circumstances in which that application, request or claim may be made, the document may be submitted or the information may be provided by other means and respecting those other means.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: The regulations may prescribe the circumstances in which the Minister may require a foreign national or another individual who, or an entity that, makes an application, request or claim, submits any document or provides information under this Act to do so using any means that are specified by the Minister.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: The regulations may

label: (a)
heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: require that payments that are required to be made or evidence of payment that is required to be provided under this Act must be made or provided by means of an electronic system;

label: (b)
heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: include provisions respecting such a system, respecting the circumstances in which those payments may be made or evidence of payments may be provided by other means, and respecting those other means; and

label: (c)
heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: include provisions respecting the date and time when, and the place where, an electronic payment or evidence of payment is deemed to be sent or received.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: The regulations may incorporate by reference the standards or specifications of any government, person or organization, either as they exist on a specified date or as amended from time to time.

heading_path: PART 4.1 Electronic Administration
own_text: If any provision of this Act or the regulations authorizes an officer or another individual to require a foreign national or another individual or an entity to submit a visa or other document or to provide information, the officer or individual is not precluded by this Part from requiring the foreign national, other individual or entity to submit the visa or other document or to provide the information, as the case may be, in accordance with that provision.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: For the purposes of sections 188 to 201, former Act means the Immigration Act , chapter I-2 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, and, where applicable, the regulations and rules made under it.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: The Immigration and Refugee Board continued by section 57 of the former Act is hereby continued.

marginal_note: Chairperson, Deputy Chairpersons, Assistant Deputy Chairpersons
heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: The Chairperson, Deputy Chairpersons and Assistant Deputy Chairpersons appointed under the former Act continue in the same capacity with the Board until the expiry or revocation of their respective appointments.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: A member appointed under the former Act to the Convention Refugee Determination Division or the Immigration Appeal Division continues in office as a member of the Board until the expiry or revocation of their appointment.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: The person who, on the coming into force of this section, held the office of Executive Director of the Board is deemed to have been appointed to that office under section 158, without prejudice to any salary and benefits he or she may receive by virtue of having held that office before that coming into force.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: Sections 94.6, 102.001 to 102.003 and 107.1 of the former Act are, despite paragraph 274(a), deemed not to be repealed and the Minister may exercise any of the powers described in those sections with respect to any business or fund that was approved by the Minister before the coming into force of paragraph 274(a).

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: Every application, proceeding or matter under the former Act that is pending or in progress immediately before the coming into force of this section shall be governed by this Act on that coming into force.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: Every application, proceeding or matter before the Convention Refugee Determination Division under the former Act that is pending or in progress immediately before the coming into force of this section, in respect of which substantive evidence has been adduced but no decision has been made, shall be continued under the former Act by the Refugee Protection Division of the Board.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: If a notice of appeal has been filed with the Immigration Appeal Division immediately before the coming into force of this section, the appeal shall be continued under the former Act by the Immigration Appeal Division of the Board.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: Every application, proceeding or matter before the Adjudication Division under the former Act that is pending or in progress immediately before the coming into force of this section, in respect of which substantive evidence has been adduced but no decision has been made, shall be continued under this Act by the Immigration Division of the Board.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: In cases referred to in section 191, a decision by the Refugee Protection Division following a hearing that has been commenced by the Convention Refugee Determination Division is not subject to an appeal under section 110.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: A decision made by the Convention Refugee Determination Division before the coming into force of this section is not subject to an appeal under section 110.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: Despite section 192, an appeal made to the Immigration Appeal Division before the coming into force of this section shall be discontinued if the appellant has not been granted a stay under the former Act and the appeal could not have been made because of section 64 of this Act.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: Despite section 192, if an appellant who has been granted a stay under the former Act breaches a condition of the stay, the appellant shall be subject to the provisions of section 64 and subsection 68(4) of this Act.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: The Refugee Protection Division has jurisdiction to consider decisions of the Convention Refugee Determination Division that are set aside by the Federal Court, the Federal Court of Appeal or the Supreme Court of Canada, and shall dispose of those matters in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: Sections 112 to 114 apply to a redetermination of a decision set aside by the Federal Court with respect to an application for landing as a member of the post-determination refugee claimants in Canada class within the meaning of the Immigration Regulations, 1978 .

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: Subsection 31(1) does not apply with respect to persons who were permanent residents, within the meaning of the former Act, on the coming into force of this section.

heading_path: PART 5 Transitional Provisions, Consequential and Related Amendments, Coordinating Amendments, Repeals and Coming into Force > Transitional Provisions
own_text: The regulations may provide for measures regarding the transition between the former Act and this Act, including measures regarding classes of persons who will be subject in whole or in part to this Act or the former Act and measures regarding financial and enforcement matters.
